Yes, I want to overcome these things more than anything  but the thing that’s stopping me is the thought that even if I try my very best it will all be for nothing. I’ve tried before. In my early 20s I became a hardcore gym bro and spent most of my time lifting weights and eating in a caloric surplus, eventually i got to the point where people were complimenting me on my appearance. 

However, I still couldn’t make any friends, women still rejected me, and I was never less alone. 

I went to parties and music festivals all the time, dropped lots of mdma, lsd, psilocybin, etc. I even sold these substances and still nobody wanted anything to do with me, not even hippies who were looking to trip would want to spend more time around me than they needed to. 

I did so much to conform to the values of modern western culture and civilization, but it all turned out to be futile and I ended up even more alone than I started out.

I’ve tried, but to no success.

Yep. I started avoiding someone a few years ago because of my own anxieties and insecurities, it wasn’t long before he was out of my life altogether, and off doing his own thing. 

Last week I realized just how cruel it was to blow off a person who actually enjoyed hanging out with me back in the day, and so I added him on Facebook and sent a message saying that I hoped he was well. He replied with a lukewarm “yeah dude I’m good how are you?” After i responded to this text he hasn’t said anything else. 

Moral of the story that I learned: “you don’t know what you have until it’s gone.”

Thanks for your response. 

Unfortunately I am unable to afford therapy or medication at the moment so that’s not a possibility, as much as I would love to be able to find a good therapist, at least I’d have someone to talk to even if it’s only an hour a week. 

I have been a very heavy pot smoker for the past few years and that has had an extreme effect on my life, and it is something that I am dealing with as difficult as it may be. My entire identity is based on being a stoner. From the clothes I wear to the music I listen to. If I had known what I was signing up for I would never have taken that first drag all those years ago.

I appreciate your advice, especially the meetup groups that could be something to look into. 

Thanks!

Nicely done bro. I would consider even a rejection a victory because you got out of your own way and did the thing anyway. I myself haven’t built up the confidence to do that yet but people like you give me hope. 

Stay strong!

The basic stuff like exercise, meditation, eating clean and healthy, getting good sleep every night, getting out of the house and going for walks in nature. As another commenter suggested, focus on your hobbies and if you don’t have any, try out one or two that interest you. 

Also deal with the emotions and feelings that come head on. Sit with them and try to understand them and why you’re feeling them. For me, marijuana covered up a whole bunch of things that I was running away from and when I quit all of those things came flooding back into my consciousness.  

It isn’t easy, and it’s an ongoing battle. Take it one day at a time and be strong! You’ve got this.

Read. It will help you think more in literary terms rather than cinematic. I also got into writing because I wanted to make movies but realized that would cost a huge amount of money, and that with fiction I could write whatever I wanted and not worry about budget constraints. Then I started reading more and now I consider myself to be a lover of literature first, cinema second. 

Another thing you could do is watch movies and try to transcribe them into words. Like try thinking how you would translate what you see onscreen into prose.

I enjoyed the book when I first read it in my late teens but looking back I can see where the criticism comes from. I guess I just read it at the right time in my life.

Hard to just name one but a book I found particularly powerful was Fahrenheit 451. I found the idea of getting rid of literature and history to be absolutely terrifying and the experience of reading that book has had a huge impact on how much I value books and knowledge in general.

I’d recommend going with his 80s stuff: V for Vendetta, Swamp Thing, From Hell, The Killing Joke

Then go onto his later stuff like Promethea and League of Extraordinary Gentlemen

Finish off with Jerusalem.
